meta.scope: South Korea Batch 7 — Remaining major environmental conventions, deeper BIT/investment-treaty detail, and digital-trade / digital-economy agreements (DEPA, Korea–Singapore Digital Partnership, EU–Korea digital pact, and related). Completes the international environmental, investment and digital layers under the locked definition.
meta.strategy_note: User requested remaining environmental conventions, more BITs detail, and digital-trade agreements. Focuses on high-citation instruments rather than exhaustive enumeration of every BIT.

candidates.title: Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer and Montreal Protocol
candidates.description: Korea is party to the Vienna Convention and the Montreal Protocol (and subsequent amendments) on substances that deplete the ozone layer. These instruments drive domestic controls on ODS and related industrial regulation.
referenced_by: Domestic ODS control regulations and industrial compliance statistics
Environmental white papers and international reporting
candidates.notes: Core atmospheric-protection instrument. Continuously cited in chemical and industrial-environmental policy.

candidates.title: Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes
candidates.description: Korea is party to the Basel Convention governing transboundary movements of hazardous wastes and their disposal. Frames domestic waste-management and export/import controls.
candidates.notes: Key waste-and-chemicals instrument alongside Rotterdam and Stockholm Conventions.

candidates.title: CITES and Ramsar Convention (Wetlands)
candidates.description: Korea is party to CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species) and the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands. These underpin wildlife-trade controls and the designation/management of Ramsar sites.
referenced_by: National biodiversity and wetland policy documents
candidates.notes: Complements the CBD/BBNJ cluster with species-trade and wetland-specific instruments.

candidates.title: Stockholm Convention (POPs) and Rotterdam Convention (PIC)
candidates.description: Korea is party to the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants and the Rotterdam Convention on Prior Informed Consent for certain hazardous chemicals and pesticides. Domestic POPs Control Act and related regulations implement these obligations.
candidates.notes: Closes the major chemicals-and-waste environmental convention set.

candidates.title: United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD)
candidates.description: Korea is party to the UNCCD. While domestic desertification risk is limited, the Convention is relevant to international cooperation, land-degradation neutrality and Korea’s overseas development and environmental assistance.
referenced_by: International cooperation and ODA environmental components
candidates.notes: Completes the set of major Rio and related environmental conventions (UNFCCC/Paris, CBD, UNCCD).

candidates.title: Bilateral Investment Treaty network — detailed status and major partners
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Republic of Korea
candidates.description: As of mid-2025 Korea had concluded BITs with approximately 101 countries/territories (84 in force, a small number not yet in force, and some terminated or replaced). Major partners include early European treaties (Germany, UK, France, etc.), Japan, China, Vietnam, and a wide set of Asian, African, Middle-Eastern and Latin-American counterparts. Many newer FTAs contain investment chapters that interact with or supersede older BITs.
referenced_by: FTA investment chapters and ISDS-related analysis
candidates.notes: Deepens the earlier BIT-network node with concrete scale and partner composition. The network is a structural feature of Korea’s outward-investment and FDI-protection architecture.

candidates.title: Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (DEPA) — Korea membership
candidates.publisher: DEPA Parties (Chile, New Zealand, Singapore + Korea)
candidates.description: Korea joined the Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (originally Chile–New Zealand–Singapore) as its first new member in 2024. DEPA is a stand-alone digital-economy agreement covering data flows, digital trade facilitation, consumer protection, and related modular rules.
referenced_by: Subsequent digital-economy negotiations and comparative analyses
candidates.notes: Key digital-trade instrument. Complements traditional FTA e-commerce chapters with a dedicated high-standard digital agreement.

candidates.title: Korea–Singapore Digital Partnership Agreement (KSDPA)
candidates.publisher: Governments of the Republic of Korea and Singapore
candidates.description: Bilateral digital-economy agreement that builds on the existing Korea–Singapore FTA and sets high-standard rules on cross-border data flows, digital trade facilitation, and related issues.
referenced_by: Digital-trade policy papers and FTA digital-chapter comparisons
candidates.notes: Important bilateral digital instrument that sits alongside DEPA and the digital components of larger FTAs.

candidates.title: EU–Korea Digital Trade Agreement
candidates.publisher: European Union and Republic of Korea
candidates.description: Digital trade agreement signed to supplement the existing Korea–EU FTA. Facilitates cross-border data flows, recognition of electronic contracts and signatures, and consumer protection in digital trade.
referenced_by: EU and Korean digital-trade and services-trade analysis
candidates.notes: Recent high-standard digital supplement to the Korea–EU FTA. Reinforces the digital layer of Korea’s European commercial relationship.

candidates.title: Korea’s digital-trade agreement architecture (overview)
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources / related agencies
candidates.description: Overview node situating DEPA, the Korea–Singapore Digital Partnership Agreement, the EU–Korea Digital Trade Agreement, digital chapters inside KORUS/RCEP/other FTAs, and ongoing interest in CPTPP digital rules. Reflects Korea’s multi-track approach to digital-economy rule-making.
referenced_by: Digital-trade policy strategies and comparative studies
candidates.notes: Meta-node that parallels the FTA-network overview. Makes explicit that Korea pursues digital rules both inside traditional FTAs and through dedicated digital-economy agreements.
